prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project manages its release lifecycle using a defined schedule for Long Term Support (LTS) versions. After a release is designated as LTS, it goes through two distinct phases: Active LTS and Maintenance LTS. 

According to the official Node.js Release working group documentation, an Active LTS phase lasts for 18 months, and the Maintenance LTS phase lasts for 12 months. 

Here are the specific citations and quotes from the official Node.js release schedule:

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-plan | QUOTE: "Active LTS: 18 months" | CLAIM: The Active LTS phase lasts for 18 months.
SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-plan | QUOTE: "Maintenance LTS: 12 months" | CLAIM: The Maintenance LTS phase lasts for 12 months.

*(Note: The same repository also summarizes this total duration in the README text: "LTS releases are supported for 30 months", which aligns with the 18 months of Active plus 12 months of Maintenance.)*
